editorial:
Imagine spending years of your life preparing for one big goal, only to realize you might be making a huge mistake. That is exactly what you get with this story. You follow a young man in Venice who is almost ready to become a priest in a Jesuit monastery. Everything seems set in stone, but as the big day gets closer, he starts to panic. The movie feels very personal and quiet, focusing on the heavy weight of making a choice that changes your entire life forever. You can really feel his stress as he tries to figure out if he is following a true calling or just running away from the real world.

The acting is top-notch because it keeps things grounded and real rather than overly dramatic. While the pace is slow, it works because it lets you sit with the character's anxiety. If you like fast action, this is not for you, but if you love a deep character study, you will enjoy it. You should definitely try to find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to soak in the beautiful Venice scenery. If that is not an option, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to go, or you can grab the Blu-ray for your physical collection.
endingExplained: By the end, the young man cannot ignore his doubts any longer. He realizes that he cannot honestly commit his life to the church while feeling so conflicted inside. Instead of going through with the ordination, he chooses to leave the monastery. It is a sad but honest conclusion where he accepts that his path lies outside the priesthood, choosing his own truth over the expectations of others.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about faith and personal struggle.
